presentingComplaint: Brought to the emergency department obtunded after a witnessed generalised seizure, preceded by 3 days of confusion, dark urine and easy bruising.
history: 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypothyroidism, previously independent. Over 5 days she developed increasing lethargy, fluctuating confusion and slurred speech, which the family initially attributed to a 'stroke'. In the last 48 hours she passed cola-coloured urine, developed spontaneous bruises over the limbs and bled from the gums after brushing. This morning she had a generalised tonic-clonic seizure at home lasting 2 minutes and did not fully regain consciousness. No preceding diarrhoea, no recent new drugs, no fever documented at home, no history of similar episodes. Not pregnant (post-menopausal). No recent chemotherapy, transplant or quinine use.
examination: Critically ill, GCS 9 (E2 V2 M5), pale with scleral icterus. Scattered petechiae over both shins and forearms with fresh gum bleeding. Transient right-sided pronator drift noted between episodes of agitation; no fixed dense hemiparesis. No neck stiffness. No splenomegaly. Cardiovascular exam reveals a soft gallop; chest clear. No focal source of sepsis identified.
imaging: CT head: no haemorrhage, no established infarct, no mass - findings out of proportion to depressed conscious level, consistent with a diffuse microvascular process rather than a single territorial stroke.
microbiology: Blood cultures no growth at 48h; malaria antigen and thick/thin films negative x2; leptospira and dengue serology negative. Stool not diarrhoeal; Shiga-toxin testing not indicated.
differentialDiagnoses: Immune (acquired) thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura - ADAMTS13 <10% with inhibitor
Disseminated intravascular coagulation secondary to sepsis
finalDiagnosis: Acquired (immune) thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura presenting as a critical thrombotic microangiopathy with encephalopathy, cardiac involvement and life-threatening thrombocytopenia (ADAMTS13 <5%, inhibitor positive).
citations: ISTH - Guidelines for diagnosis and management of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, 2020
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Thrombotic Microangiopathies (TTP/HUS)
stewardship: Non-infective thrombotic microangiopathy; no empiric antibiotics indicated once malaria and sepsis are reasonably excluded. Definitive therapy is urgent therapeutic plasma exchange with corticosteroids and caplacizumab; rituximab for immune TTP.
contraindications: Platelet transfusion is contraindicated in TTP except for immediately life-threatening haemorrhage - it can precipitate further microvascular thrombosis
Do not delay plasma exchange while awaiting ADAMTS13 results
Avoid empiric anticoagulation for the raised D-dimer - this is a platelet-consumptive TMA, not primary DIC
edgeCases: Normal/near-normal coagulation (INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) with severe thrombocytopenia and MAHA distinguishes TTP from DIC
Renal impairment is mild and neurology dominant, favouring TTP over typical (Shiga-toxin) HUS
Elevated troponin reflects cardiac microvascular involvement and marks a poor prognosis in severe TTP
If ADAMTS13 were normal, reconsider atypical HUS / complement-mediated TMA
expectedMaiK: Blood-film-confirmed MAHA plus severe thrombocytopenia with no better explanation IS TTP until proven otherwise - start therapeutic plasma exchange and steroids emergently, calculate a PLASMIC score, send ADAMTS13 before PEX, and withhold platelet transfusion.
expectedNextQuestions: Are there schistocytes on the peripheral blood film?
Any recent diarrhoeal illness, drugs (quinine, clopidogrel), pregnancy, autoimmune disease or malignancy?
Are coagulation studies (INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) normal to exclude DIC?
Has an ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor sample been drawn before plasma exchange?
expectedInvestigations: LDH, haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin, reticulocyte count
Coagulation profile: INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer
ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor (before plasma exchange)
Troponin and ECG for cardiac involvement
regressionAssertions: MAHA (schistocytes, high LDH, undetectable haptoglobin, negative Coombs) with severe thrombocytopenia is recognised as TTP
Normal INR/aPTT/fibrinogen is used to exclude DIC
Therapeutic plasma exchange + steroids recommended emergently without waiting for ADAMTS13
No empiric antibiotics recommended for this non-infective TMA
